title: Removing the top one percent of partial-leverage records left ozone and warmth intervals across zero in four US bird samples in 1995-2024
abstract: We tested whether a published ozone by seasonal warmth slope depends on records with high partial leverage. We reused four US bird survey samples and the same model. We selected records from predictors alone, then removed the top 1% or 5% and fit all controls and fixed effects again. Removing the top 1% left all four intervals adjusted for four samples across zero. In the early West, 21 surveys supplied 32.6% of original partial leverage. Removal changed the slope from -0.551 to -0.437 recorded species per 10 ppb ozone and 2 C warmth. Its adjusted interval changed from -1.091 to -0.010 to -1.136 to +0.263. Removing the top 5% kept the early western slope negative at -0.765, with an interval across zero. Thus, the negative sign persisted but a clear adjusted interval did not. High leverage does not show data error. Deletion changes exposure support and can remove valid extreme conditions. These are sensitivity tests on shared source records, not independent biological replication or causal climate estimates. Survey selection, detection bias, coarse exposure and few western state clusters remain limits. The package includes code, the source panel, hashes, aggregate results and numerical checks.

display.caption: Refits after removal of records with the largest partial leverage. Bars give intervals adjusted for four samples. The right panel shows the original partial leverage removed. Deletion is a diagnostic, not a preferred estimate.
